My favourite Mac transcription tool, MacWhisper, has received another major update today, adding live meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker identification, deeper Apple Intelligence integration, and brand-new transcription models. Here's what's in the update.

Deeper integration between MacWhisper and Apple Intelligence

I've written many articles about my reliance on MacWhisper, particularly within my podcast production workflow.

MacWhisper is one of the earliest AI transcription tools built for Mac. Since its launch in 2023 by independent developer Jordi Bruin, it has been continuously improved, with ever-expanding support for new models, services, and workflows.

These improvements have spanned automatic meeting recording and speaker identification, folder watching, system-wide dictation, local and cloud AI models, as well as integrations with services like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today, MacWhisper upgrades to version 15.2, introducing improved speaker identification powered by NVIDIA's newly released Nemotron 3 speaker diarisation model.

This change also brings another major feature in this update: live meeting transcription.

This feature had been on MacWhisper's public roadmap for some time and has now finally been realised, allowing users to view live, rewind, copy, or send live transcripts during meetings in progress.

On the actual transcription model front, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model, supporting 22 languages, along with deeper integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts in macOS 27.

Now, Mac users (including those in the EU) can search transcripts system-wide, open them with Siri, pass text into Shortcuts, and reference on-screen transcripts within Siri or Apple Intelligence queries.

Lastly, MacWhisper 15.2 adds folders and subfolders to help organise transcripts and meetings, and supports dragging existing transcript files into folders from the sidebar.
